answer: The defence rests on beekeeper association tenure with apiary inspection logs: apiary inspections passed with one association yearly. Forging 328 of these means building 328 separate inspection logs from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. Call it the sonnet rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the dune record is open for audit, and the knoll window is too short for 328 aliases to earn their price back.
